name: Ernie Els
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 1994 U.S. Open at Oakmont at age 24, capturing his first major championship and establishing himself as a global force in professional golf.
early_history_summary: Els grew up playing multiple sports in Germiston, South Africa, learning golf from his father at age 8. He won the World Junior Golf Championship at 14, became the youngest South African Amateur winner at 16, and turned professional at 20, quickly dominating the Sunshine Tour before winning the 1994 U.S. Open at 24.
family_context_summary: Born in Johannesburg to a middle-class family; father Neels was a trucking executive, mother Hettie was a homemaker. Grew up in Lambton, Germiston with an older brother.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father Neels played golf recreationally and introduced Ernie to the game at age 8 at the Germiston Golf course, providing early instruction and access.
primary_early_advantage_tags: father-taught golf, scratch golfer at 14, World Junior champion, South African golf pipeline
evidence_summary: Ernie Els grew up in a middle-class South African family where his father Neels, a trucking executive, introduced him to golf at age 8. A multi-sport athlete, Els won the World Junior Golf Championship at 14 and became the youngest South African Amateur winner at 16. He turned professional at 20 and won six of eight Sunshine Tour events in 1992, then captured the 1994 U.S. Open at age 24. His father's golf involvement and the strong South African golf tradition provided early domain exposure and pipeline access, while his mother's ban on contact sports after a rugby injury channeled his athletic gifts toward golf.
starting_point: Born to a middle-class family in Johannesburg, South Africa; father was a trucking executive who played golf recreationally.
current_position: Former World No. 1 golfer with 79 professional wins and 4 major championships; active on PGA Tour Champions; resides in Florida, England, and South Africa.

name: Kevin Berry
milestone_by_age_26: Won three gold medals at the 1962 British Empire and Commonwealth Games at age 17 while setting world butterfly records, then won Olympic gold in the 200m butterfly at the 1964 Tokyo Olympics at age 19.
early_history_summary: Berry grew up in working-class Sydney, taught to swim by his elder sister at Botany Bay. He joined the Pyrmont Club at 11, reached the Olympic butterfly final at 15 in 1960, won three Commonwealth Games golds at 17 while setting world records, and won Olympic gold at 19 in 1964 under coaches Don Talbot and James Counsilman.
family_context_summary: Born in Sydney, Australia, the second of seven children in a working-class family with no prior sporting background. Father Frederick was a bar manager who immigrated to Australia in the 1920s.

evidence_summary: Kevin Berry grew up in a working-class Sydney family with no sporting background; his father was a bar manager. He reached the Olympic butterfly final at 15 in 1960, won three gold medals at the 1962 Commonwealth Games at 17 while setting world records, and won Olympic gold at 19 in 1964. His trajectory was propelled by access to two legendary coaches — Don Talbot in Australia and James Counsilman at Indiana University — representing an elite performance pipeline.

name: Jil Sander
milestone_by_age_26: Opened her first fashion boutique in Hamburg in 1968 at age 24, founding the Jil Sander label with her mother's sewing machine and launching her career as a fashion designer.
early_history_summary: Sander studied textile engineering in Krefeld, attended UCLA as an exchange student, and worked as a fashion writer at McCall's in New York before family deaths brought her back to Hamburg. At 24, she opened her first boutique in 1968 using her mother's sewing machine, founding the Jil Sander label and selling her own designs alongside established European designers.
family_context_summary: Born in Wesselburen, Germany during WWII; father Walter was a locksmith who fought on the Russian front. Parents divorced when she was six months old; mother Erna-Anna later remarried a car dealer named Erik Libuda.

evidence_summary: Jil Sander grew up in postwar Germany; her father, a locksmith, left when she was an infant and her mother later remarried. She studied textile engineering at Krefeld, attended UCLA as an exchange student, and worked as a fashion writer at McCall's magazine in New York. After family deaths brought her back to Hamburg, she opened her first boutique at age 24 in 1968 using her mother's sewing machine, founding the Jil Sander label. Her early advantage came from deep domain immersion through textile engineering education and fashion journalism, rather than family wealth or connections.
starting_point: Born in wartime Germany to a locksmith father who left when she was an infant; mother later remarried a car dealer.
current_position: Retired fashion designer; founded and built the Jil Sander brand into a global luxury label; brand continues under new ownership.

He attended the University of Colorado on a baseball scholarship but left, drifting through oil field work and European art study before enrolling at the American Academy of Dramatic Arts in New York. He made his Broadway debut in 1959 at age 22, earned an Emmy nomination at 25 for 'The Voice of Charlie Pont,' and had his first credited film role in 'War Hunt' (1962). Personal adversity — his mother's death and the loss of his firstborn — channeled his intensity into acting.

early_history_summary: Kapuściński grew up in poverty in Pinsk (now Belarus), the son of primary school teachers displaced by WWII. He began working as a journalist at 19 for Sztandar Mlodych, earned a history degree from the University of Warsaw at 20, and was sent to Africa by the Polish Press Agency at 25 as a foreign correspondent covering decolonization.
family_context_summary: Born in Pinsk (now Belarus) to Maria and Józef Kapuściński, both primary school teachers. Born into poverty in a polyglot, multi-ethnic region; family displaced during WWII.

primary_early_advantage_tags: poverty, WWII displacement, early journalism start, foreign correspondent at 25
evidence_summary: Ryszard Kapuściński was born into poverty in Pinsk (now Belarus) to primary school teacher parents, growing up during WWII in a war-torn region. He began working as a journalist at 19 for Sztandar Mlodych and earned a history degree from the University of Warsaw at 20. At 25, the Polish Press Agency sent him to Africa as a foreign correspondent, where he covered decolonization and 27 revolutions over his career. His early advantages were minimal — extreme poverty and wartime displacement were the dominant forces, creating urgency and a distinctive outsider perspective that defined his reporting.

current_position: Died on January 23, 2007 in Warsaw at age 74; final role: celebrated author and journalist, considered one of the greatest reportage writers of the 20th century.

name: Antonio Gades
milestone_by_age_26: Promoted to principal dancer in Pilar López's Ballet Español at age 18 in 1955, after just one season in the company, touring world stages with one of Spain's premier dance troupes.

evidence_summary: Antonio Gades was born into a working-class family in Elda, Spain; his father was a mosaic floor layer and communist who fought for the Republic. Gades left school at 11 to work menial jobs and began dancing at 15, initially 'from hunger.' He was spotted by legendary flamenco dancer Pilar López, who invited him to join her Ballet Español at 17, renamed him, and personally trained him in flamenco, classical ballet, and folk dance. Within one season, López promoted him to principal dancer at age 18, and he toured world stages for nine years. His early advantage was almost entirely mentor-driven, with López providing the training, platform, and artistic formation that launched his career.
starting_point: Born into a working-class family in Elda, Spain; father was a mosaic floor layer and communist, mother worked in footwear manufacturing.
current_position: Died on July 20, 2004 in Madrid at age 67; final role: legendary flamenco dancer and choreographer, co-founder and artistic director of the Ballet Nacional de España.
